title: Count Even and Odd
statement: Count even and odd numbers in an array.
inputOutputContract: Output counts as even odd, separated by one space; 0 is even.

mistakes.hint1: Inspect the swaps parity condition behavior in countEvenOdd; the current algorithm is close, but one operation changes its result.
mistakes.hint2: Start by tracing T1 manually. Watch array indices / comparisons / loop boundaries / return values at each iteration or recursive return.
mistakes.hint3: Check the invariant of countEvenOdd: Count zero as even and update exactly one of the two counters for each element.
mistakes.hint4: Concentrate on the expression or branch that controls this mistake: `if (arr[i] % 2 != 0)`. What does it do on the failing input?
mistakes.hint5: Compare the intermediate state with the expected output of T1. The mistake is in swaps parity condition, not merely formatting.
mistakes.hint6: Adjust the faulty operation so that it follows this rule: Count zero as even and update exactly one of the two counters for each element.
mistakes.hint7: A targeted correction is to replace `if (arr[i] % 2 != 0)` with `if (arr[i] % 2 == 0)` in countEvenOdd, then retest T1–T6.
